name: Plugins
summary: Install a ready-made bundle of skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers as one unit.
what: A plugin is a directory that packages several extensions together, usually with a manifest file that names it. Most plugins come from a marketplace, which is a catalog listing plugins and where to fetch them. Each piece also works alone; a plugin is for when you want them installed, updated and shared together.

impact.title: One install for a whole setup
impact.detail: Get a configuration someone else built with a single command, and receive its updates from the marketplace.

impact.title: Share your own setup
impact.detail: Package your skills, subagents and hooks to give them to teammates or reuse them across projects.

impact.title: Easy to switch off
impact.detail: A plugin can be disabled without uninstalling it. This matters because an enabled plugin takes part in every session.

howItWorks: Run /plugin in a Claude Code terminal session.
Browse the Discover tab, which lists the plugins from your marketplaces, and install one.
Claude Code loads everything in the plugin: its skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers.
A plugin skill runs under the plugin's name, in the form /plugin-name:skill-name.
Disable a plugin from /plugin, or with claude plugin disable in your shell, to stop it without removing it.

events.note: The plugin system was released, with marketplaces and the /plugin command.
